PARTIAL — one of this acknowledgement's two legs, and it is the load-bearing one. The ack accepts 64 undeclared module couplings as correct, and cites as measured evidence: 'lifted to subsystem it reads 11 couplings, 11 covered, 0 uncovered.' That subsystem roll-up came from lift_to_level choosing a containment parent by id prefix, which silently dropped every module contained by a `sub:*` subsystem. THE ZERO WAS AN ARTEFACT. Corrected 2026-08-30: 19 couplings, 13 covered, SIX uncovered — sub:change-and-structure<->sub:finding, <->sub:telling, sub:evidence<->sub:finding, <->sub:telling, sub:evidence<->sys:time-history, sub:finding<->sub:telling.

THE OTHER LEG STILL STANDS and is why this is not a withdrawal: 'all 64 pairs sit inside ONE crate with zero crossing a crate boundary, and 44 of the 55 files in reflow2-core carry impl DesignGraph' — measured independently of the roll-up, unaffected by this defect, and still the right reason not to write 64 module-level contracts.

WHAT IS OWED: a re-reading, not an automatic reversal. The rule the ack invokes (a contract is declared at the lowest level and higher levels answer by roll-up) is unchanged; what changed is that the roll-up now says six subsystem boundaries do NOT answer. Whether those six are real contracts or another correct absence is the owner's judgement, and nothing here decides it.
